title: Agent Frameworks Considered Harmful — Rémi Louf, .txt
talk_summary: Rémi Louf built a minimal agent runtime over two weeks: markdown-defined agents, cron/event triggers, an append-only event log, and content-addressed prompts (hashes of system prompt, skills, tools, user message) enabling exact replay and diffs. He argues frameworks hide what the model actually saw, and that typed tool calls and typed events between agents make bad actions impossible rather than unlikely.

takeaways.what_they_do: Store each prompt part (system prompt, skill descriptions, tool descriptions, user message) as a hash-addressed component and represent the rendered prompt as a list of hashes, so any model output traces back to exactly what entered context.

takeaways.technique: Replay runs against a different model
takeaways.what_they_do: Because requests are rebuildable from the content-addressed graph, replay the identical request against another model to check output quality before switching providers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can rebuild the request from the graph, and you can just replay it exactly the same ... you can use a different model

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents declare accepted and emitted event types; triggers are events (new voice note, new PR, new email) rather than only schedules, so topology emerges from subscriptions with no edges to maintain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All you need is events. You have no edges to maintain. Agents simply subscribe to events.
takeaways.numbers: 20 agents deployed after a month, many contributed by non-technical staff

takeaways.technique: Typed tool calls and typed events as hard boundaries
takeaways.what_they_do: Enforce schemas at the two boundaries — agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent — so invalid tool calls and malformed inter-agent messages are rejected structurally, not just discouraged by prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the job of the kernel is actually to make bad actions impossible not just unlikely
takeaways.numbers: ~20% of events were wrong/rejected before switching to structured outputs

takeaways.what_they_do: One append-only events table records everything with causal links (which event triggered which), queryable for debugging multi-agent runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you only have one append only events table ... They are causally linked as well ... super useful when you're debugging

takeaways.technique: Markdown agent definitions over code frameworks
takeaways.what_they_do: Define agents as versioned markdown files dropped in a folder; runtime picks them up, so prompts are diffable, reviewable in PRs, and editable by non-engineers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can version it, you can diff it, you can review in the PR ... you drop it in a folder, and then it just magically appears
